deployment.entry: harness/index.html — the PROJECT(1).md §9 M1 minimal inference harness page
deployment.scope: core runtime + harness wrapper; PWA not built

harnessOnlyBytes.bundled: not separable in the current bundle: harness/dist/main.js is one esbuild output combining harness/src/main.ts, packages/core/dist and the onnxruntime-web JS glue, so the harness wrapper's share of those bytes is not isolated. The bundle total is not the eventual PWA's total.

deployment.servedBy: harness/serve.mjs — one same-origin HTTP/1.1 origin on 127.0.0.1, no reverse proxy
deployment.cacheContract: cache-control: no-cache + ETag revalidation (serve.mjs cacheMode=validate, added by ticket 08; the default stays no-store)
deployment.contentEncoding: identity — nothing is compressed, so wire bytes equal file bytes
deployment.appScript: harness/dist/main.js: esbuild ESM bundle of packages/core/dist plus onnxruntime-web/dist/ort.wasm.bundle.min.mjs (77,024 bytes of runtime JS glue). Not minified at the core layer, and not the PWA — tickets 10a and 10 do not exist yet.
deployment.sourceMaps: harness/dist/main.js.map exists but a headless page without devtools never requests it
deployment.threads: ORT runs on the WASM execution provider with 4 threads under COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation (serve.mjs sets both headers)

cold.description: Cold start — first visit, empty cache

warm.description: Warm visit — same browser, assets revalidated from cache

repeat.description: supplementary — second inference in the same page, sessions warm

measurement.byteCounting: summed from the origin's own request log (harness/serve.mjs), which sees WASM and worker loads that page resource timings do not; HTTP header bytes are excluded
measurement.timingAnchor: performance.timeOrigin of the measured document. appReadyMs is the instant the page was handed to the driver to attach the image, so it carries one Playwright round-trip; harnessLatencyMs reports the polling lag on the other side of the run.
measurement.centralValue: median, with min and max published beside it. With n=5 no percentile is claimed.
measurement.latencyBases: cold and warm are timed from their own navigation, page load included; the repeat phase has no navigation and is the duration from the receipt being handed over to the result arriving, with everything already in memory. That is why the repeat row carries no app-ready or OCR-ready figure.

image.note: user data, not app footprint: it is never a network request (the page reads the File object directly). Declared because it sets the inference time.

excludedFromFootprint: the receipt image itself — user data, and never a network request
HTTP request/response header bytes (a few hundred bytes per asset per visit)
anything a service worker would cache: this deployment has no service worker yet (ticket 17), so the HTTP cache is the whole cache
notMeasured: any real phone, tablet or low-end laptop — the 4x class is an emulated CPU rate, not a device
network latency and bandwidth beyond loopback; on a real link add RTT and whatever the connection delivers, which is why bytes are published per asset and not only as a total
peak memory: the WASM heap, the decoded image buffers and both inference graphs are resident after load and are not sized here
parse() and validate() separately: they run in the same frame as inference on this page, so firstResultMs includes them and modelLoadMs does not
PP-OCRv6 Small, quantized builds, or a lazy/deferred model load (1E.3, ticket 09b, and the risk R2 contingencies)

findings.detail: Chromium HTTP cache retains ~6-8 MiB per entity; the 14.85 MB ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm answers 200 with full body on every warm visit, while 7 of 8 assets revalidate as 304
findings.evidence: session probe: 6 MiB entity retained, 8 MiB entity not retained, same server/headers as harness; 512 MB disk cache rules out eviction
findings.remedy: ticket 17 Cache API; header changes cannot fix browser per-entity limits
findings.affectsClaim: section 9 initial-download / re-fetch cost, not the local-processing claim (same-origin only)

provenance.supersedes: the withdrawn "~4.3 MB complete OCR pipeline" claim (ADR-002, PROJECT(1).md §2). The claim stays withdrawn; this file carries the measured number.
provenance.note: measuredAt and the request log are the record of one run on one machine. Latency is not a stable constant: it is a distribution of n samples on the declared class, and a different machine class will produce a different table.
